description: ACCTFILE reaches the declared-but-dead M03B-WRITE operation, which performs no I/O at all and reports the stale FILE STATUS the preceding keyed read left in the file's own status area. Three calls in one session: OPEN INPUT, a keyed READ-K whose key is absent from the seeded rows, then 'W'. THE ARM. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD (app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118) tests its arms in source order - 'TRNXFILE' (:119), 'XREFFILE' (:121), 'CUSTFILE' (:123), then 'ACCTFILE' (:125) - and :126 performs 4000-ACCTFILE-PROC THRU 4999-EXIT. Reaching the fourth arm is evidence that the three earlier names were tested and rejected without control falling into WHEN OTHER (:127-128), whose GO TO 9999-GOBACK jumps past every nnn900-EXIT and would therefore leave LK-M03B-RC stale rather than set. Arm order is behaviour, not presentation (gate G30, rule R7). CALL 1 - THE OPEN. IF M03B-OPEN (:208) is true, so OPEN INPUT ACCT-FILE (:209) runs and GO TO 4900-EXIT (:210) leaves the paragraph before any later guard is reached; 4900-EXIT (:225-226) MOVEs ACCTFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC and 4999-EXIT (:228-229) EXITs. A successful OPEN INPUT yields '00'. CALL 2 - THE KEYED READ THAT MISSES. IF M03B-OPEN (:208) is now false and IF M03B-READ-K (:213) is true, so MOVE LK-M03B-KEY (1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) TO FD-ACCT-ID (:214) runs, then READ ACCT-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT (:215), then GO TO 4900-EXIT (:217) and :226. The key '00000000099' is absent from the two seeded rows, whose ACCT-IDs are 00000000001 and 00000000002, so the READ fails with FILE STATUS '23' - record not found - and moves nothing whatsoever into the record area. LK-M03B-FLDT therefore stays exactly as the caller left it: CBSTM03A's 3000-ACCTFILE-GET (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:392-414) issues MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:400) before every call, so this image pins 1000 spaces rather than a stale record. That is the assertion no status byte could make: a translation that returned the previously read record on a miss would still show '23' here, and only the record area would give it away. THE MOVE AT :214 IS A NUMERIC MOVE, AND THE SAME STATEMENT AT :189 IS NOT - the parity subtlety of this DD. LK-M03B-KEY (1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) is a reference modification yielding the first 11 bytes of the 25-byte key span. The receiver here, FD-ACCT-ID (:77), is PIC 9(11) - an integer numeric item - so COBOL treats the alphanumeric source as an unsigned integer and aligns it on the decimal point: right-justified, zero-filled on the LEFT, and truncated on the left had the source been longer. Eleven source bytes fill an eleven-digit receiver exactly, so the effective key is '00000000099'. The identical statement at :189 targets FD-CUST-ID (:72), which is PIC X(09) - alphanumeric - and therefore left-justifies and space-pads on the RIGHT. One statement shape, two opposite padding rules, chosen entirely by the receiver's PICTURE clause. A port that applied one rule to both DDs would satisfy the CUSTFILE cases and fail the ACCTFILE ones, or the reverse, which is why both receivers are exercised in this suite. CALL 3 - THE DEAD OPERATION. 88 M03B-WRITE VALUE 'W' is declared at :107 and is SET nowhere in app/cbl - neither CBSTM03A nor any other program ever requests it - all four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT, and no paragraph in CBSTM03B contains a WRITE statement. The operation is therefore dead code, and practice B5 requires that it stay dead rather than be quietly implemented. Gate G48 nonetheless requires every one of the six declared operation codes to be exercised, and this is the suite's only 'W' call, so the code is covered as the no-op it is rather than covered by being given behaviour. A 'W' request matches IF M03B-OPEN (:208) no, IF M03B-READ-K (:213) no, IF M03B-CLOSE (:220) no, and falls through to 4900-EXIT (:225) having performed no I/O at all; :226 then MOVEs whatever ACCTFILE-STATUS already holds, which is still the '23' the failed keyed read wrote there. Reporting '23' rather than '00' is precisely what distinguishes a genuine no-op from a call that quietly succeeded, and it is only assertable because the caller reset LK-M03B-RC to '00' beforehand - so the '23' in this image can have come from nowhere but the file's own status area. Its key span and key length are the blank and the '000{' of a non-keyed call, unchanged by the subroutine, because the dead path writes back nothing but the status. THE STATUS AREA (gate G47). ACCTFILE-STATUS (:95-97) is the fourth of four independent two-byte areas (:83-97), none of which carries a VALUE clause, so every status pinned here belongs to that area alone and says nothing about TRNXFILE-STATUS, XREFFILE-STATUS or CUSTFILE-STATUS. That independence is exactly what makes the stale '23' of call 3 meaningful: it is the same storage the READ of call 2 wrote, not a shared or re-initialised one. ACCESS MODE. ACCTFILE is ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM, RECORD KEY IS FD-ACCT-ID (:49-53), so 4000-ACCTFILE-PROC guards only M03B-OPEN, M03B-READ-K and M03B-CLOSE - there is no sequential-READ guard on this DD at all, which is why a read here is necessarily keyed. THE ZONED KEY LENGTH. LK-M03B-KEY-LN is PIC S9(4) (:111), a signed zoned item whose sign is overpunched into the low-order byte, so the width 11 renders as the image '001A' - the 'A' being a positive digit 1 - while the 0 that a non-keyed call carries renders as '000{', a positive zero. Eleven is not a chosen number: CBSTM03A:398 COMPUTEs it as LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID, and XREF-ACCT-ID is PIC 9(11) in app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy. THE WIDTHS, re-derivable by hand (practice B11). LK-M03B-AREA is 1040 = 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000 (:100-112). The ACCTFILE record is 300 = 11 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 178 from app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, and the FD split at :77-78 confirms it independently as 11 + 289. FD-ACCT-DATA is declared twice in this program - PIC X(318) at :63 inside FD-TRNXFILE-REC and PIC X(289) at :78 inside FD-ACCTFILE-REC - which is legal COBOL because the two sit in different FD records and which case16 pins side by side; the 289-byte span is the one in play here. THE RECORD DECODE. Both seeded rows are pinned across all thirteen CVACT01Y spans in declaration order rather than only as byte images, because FieldDiffer compares field by field (gate G17) and a whole-string compare would hide a misplaced boundary inside a span. ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE is misspelled in the copybook (app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy:11) and is therefore pinned misspelled: the copybook is the contract (requirement I1), and correcting the spelling here would silently unbind the field across the whole suite. The trailing FILLER X(178) (:17) is pinned as 178 spaces because omitting it would leave the record 122 bytes long instead of 300 (gates G19 and G21). THE MONEY FIELDS ARE BYTES, NOT NUMBERS. The five S9(10)V99 spans each carry a zoned sign overpunch in their low-order byte, where '{' is a positive digit zero ('{' = +0 through 'I' = +9, '}' = -0 through 'R' = -9). Row 0 therefore reads ACCT-CURR-BAL '00000001940{' = +194.00, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT '00000020200{' = +2020.00 and ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT '00000010200{' = +1020.00 at scale 2; row 1 reads +158.00, +6130.00 and +5448.00; and all four cycle amounts are '00000000000{' = +0.00. They are pinned as the twelve bytes that sit on disk rather than as normalised signed literals, and never as JSON numbers, because a decimal here must not be re-scaled or reparsed merely by being loaded - and never as double or float, neither of which can represent a PIC S9(10)V99 value exactly (rule R4). THE PRESERVED ODDITIES (practice B5). ACCT-ADDR-ZIP reads 'A000000000' and ACCT-GROUP-ID is blank in every one of the fifty fixture rows. Both are semantically odd and both are uniform, so both are pinned verbatim rather than corrected: this migration reproduces what is there, including what looks like a data-entry artefact. READ-ONLY PROOF. All four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph writes, so the seeded dataset is read back after the run and pinned row for row, unchanged, and its FINAL_STATE row count and 300-byte record length are pinned too. That is an assertion no area image could make: a subroutine that wrote through the keyed read, or that let the dead 'W' fall into a WRITE, would leave the file altered while every LK-M03B-RC still looked right. WHAT IS NOT HERE. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference and no CALL statement - it GOBACKs (:130-131) without ever touching one - and LK-M03B-RC is a FILE STATUS, not a return code. expectedMessages is empty because the program contains no DISPLAY statement at all; 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' belongs to its caller (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:407). jobParameters is empty because CBSTM03B is a @Component and not a Spring Batch Job despite the ...Job name the plan assigns it (gate G12, requirement I3), because it is never reached through a JobLauncher or over HTTP (gate G51), and because job parameters belong to a BATCH_JOB alone - the call script this case describes therefore lives beside the other nineteen in CBSTM03BParityTest, since ParityCase carries inputs and expectations but no script. No normalisation applies: acctdata rows are a full 300 bytes on disk with FILLER already space-filled, and the suite's only two pads are cardxref 36 to 50 and USRSEC 57 to 80. Every byte is US-ASCII, the code page of the authoritative app/data/ASCII fixtures, and never a platform default (practice B8). M03B-REWRITE 'Z' (:108) is the paired dead operation and is pinned by case18; the keyed read that HITS is pinned by case13, case14, case16 and case20; WHEN OTHER by case19. PROVENANCE (practice B12). Every expected value above was derived statically - by structured reading of the line numbers cited, the CVACT01Y byte offsets and the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt - and was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the COBOL. That execution is empirically impossible here: cobc refuses CBSTM03B at :114 because PROCEDURE DIVISION USING is a subprogram entry rather than an executable main, its indexed file handler is reported disabled, which excludes all four of these ORGANIZATION INDEXED files, and no Language Environment CEE service exists. AAP section 0.7.6 records the eight verified blockers and section 0.9.11 escalates the deviation as risk R-A: only the provenance of these values changes - 20 cases per program, field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module all stand.
